description: An advanced visual that shows the distribution of numeric values for several groups. Create an in-depth visualization with ridge styling, line curves, scaling, vibrant colors, conditional formatting, and more. Allow quick comparisons by effectively utilizing space in your Power BI report. A ridgeline plot, also known as a joy plot, is a data visualization used to display the distribution of numeric variables for multiple categories along a common continuous axis. It displays the distribution by stacking them vertically in such a manner that the overlapping lines create the impression of a mountain range. Ridgeline plots are particularly useful for showcasing how the patterns of distributions change across different categories, time periods, or scenarios, providing insights into the variability and trends within the data. Check out the live demo here. To access all the advanced settings features, click the gear "⚙️" icon in the top-right corner. Key Feature Highlights: Multiple Distribution: Plot distribution across several groups. It also allows more than one value comparison. Ridge Style: For visually appealing display, smooth line styling and stroke and marker options are available. Scaling: Spot patterns easily by controlling the Y-axis scaling and density/area overlaps. Colors: Apply color by axis, category. There is 30+ palettes, 7 color scheme and FX rules available.…
